subject: Production: websocket backpressure + heartbeat negotiation timeouts at OliveHealth (P1)
messages:
From: Maria Suarez <maria.suarez@olivehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:12:05 -0800
Subject: Production: live-stream truncation and websocket timeouts (urgent)

Hi Sofia —

We started seeing a production incident at ~08:00 PT this morning where clinician-facing live summaries are truncating mid-response and our clients are receiving WebSocket closure errors. Key points:
- Error-rate spike: 12% increase in generation failures since 08:00 PT (from 0.6% to 12.6%).
- Symptom: streaming responses stop emitting chunks; client eventually sees "Connection closed" or a 504 from our edge.
- Affected customers: our internal pilot (700 concurrent sessions).
- Example request id: r-OLH-20261130-8a7c; last server log attached (error_snippet.log).

This is impacting scheduled telehealth workflows. Can you escalate and confirm whether this is related to the recent runtime patch you rolled last week? We need an ETA and immediate mitigation steps.

—Maria
Maria Suarez
Head of Engineering, Olive Health
maria.suarez@olivehealth.com
+1 415 555 0132

Attachment: error_snippet.log (text)

Subject: Re: Production: live-stream truncation and websocket timeouts (urgent)

Maria — thanks for the quick flag. I'm escalating immediately and opening a P1 war room with SRE and our runtime team. Early notes:
- We're seeing correlated errors on some dedicated inference pools in us-west1; initial telemetry suggests negotiation/heartbeat failures during high-concurrency bursts.
- Immediate asks from us: a small packet capture from a failing client and the SDK version you are on (client-side WS lib). The attached ticket (incident_ticket_9847.txt) will be the tracking artifact.

Short-term mitigations you can try now (low risk):
- Switch the client to polling (non-streaming) for critical requests until we stabilize (if feasible).
- If sticking with WS, increase the client heartbeat to 2s and lower max chunk size temporarily.

I'll loop in Dylan for diagnostics and Marissa to coordinate customer comms. We'll update every 30 minutes until resolved. Apologies — we're on it.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:22:10 -0800
Subject: RE: Production: live-stream truncation and websocket timeouts (urgent)

Hi team — quick technical summary from initial triage:
- Observed anomaly: short windows of sustained connection backpressure causing the server-side send buffer to block; chunked transfer stalls when per-connection pacing crosses a threshold.
- Metric evidence: outbound token send latency spikes align with increased KV-cache miss rates on shard gw-12 (~09:00 PT). See attached svc_metrics_graph.png.
- Probable trigger: a runtime micro-optimization patch last Wednesday changed socket backlog handling and appears to reduce socket drain under sudden fanout.

Immediate remediation options (ranked):
1) Route Olive Health traffic to dedicated burst pool (no code change) — quick but requires capacity approval.
2) Roll back the backlog handling change in the runtime (30–60 min to patch + redeploy).
3) Apply a hotfix to enforce smaller chunk sizes and aggressive keepalive on affected frontends (fast, ~10–20 minutes config change).

We already captured a live trace — uploaded to console: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace-12345 (live_trace.span.txt attached). For now, I've enabled conservative backpressure throttling on a small percentage of connections to buy time; we need an exec decision on capacity burst and credits.

Dylan
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

Attachments: svc_metrics_graph.png, live_trace.span.txt

Subject: Exec brief: WebSocket negotiation + backpressure timeouts impacting Olive Health (P1) — decision needed

Markus / Marissa — summarizing for exec attention and approvals:
Impact
- Customer: Olive Health (pilot, sensitive telehealth flows) — production consumer-facing failures starting 08:00 PT.
- Symptom set: streaming responses stall mid-chunk; client sees WS closure or 504s.
- Business risk: Olive has flagged potential pause of paid usage if not remediated within business hours; this is a mid-enterprise, high-sensitivity pilot (Deal DEAL-3321-OLH).
- Metrics: 12% jump in generation error-rate; observed on 3 frontends in us-west1.

Diagnosis & technical recommendation (from SRE)
- Root cause hypothesis: regression from last-week runtime socket backlog change -> increased blocking under transient fanout; resulting in chunked transfer stalls and heartbeat negotiation timeouts.
- Immediate options: route traffic to burst pool (fast, requires capacity approval), rollback runtime patch (30–60m), or apply config hotfix to reduce chunk sizes + increase keepalive (10–20m).

Requested exec decisions / approvals
1) Approve a temporary dedicated burst allocation for Olive Health (estimate: 4 x T4 equivalent for 4 hours).
2) Approve up to 5% credit for impacted requests and a goodwill SLA credit if outage window extends beyond 2 hours.
3) Greenlight rolling back the runtime patch if SRE confirms rollback mitigates within test window.

Owners & next steps
- Dylan: run hotfix and confirm mitigation metrics (owner for step 3).
- Marissa: customer comms + credit/contract coordination.
- Sofia: handle exec communication and approval tracking.

Attachments: exec_summary_olh.pdf (one-pager), traces uploaded to console https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace-12345

Please reply with approvals asap; Marissa, can you confirm the credit band we can offer? If we don't get a capacity decision in 15 minutes, we'll proceed with the hotfix config change and keep rolling.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Sr. Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
